page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m2.xlarge is an entry-tier x86_64 server deployed on KVM hypervisors. The instance utilizes Intel Xeon processors clocked at 2.5 GHz, provisioned as 2 physical cores with hyper-threading to deliver 4 dedicated vCPUs. The CPU subsystem is backed by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside hardware instruction support for AVX, AVX-512, BMI2, and AES-NI cryptographic acceleration. Memory capacity is fixed at 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation (2.0 GB per vCPU). The configuration does not include local disk storage, requiring network-attached volumes for persistent data, and features no GPU acceleration. Networking is provisioned with a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth, without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate steady single-threaded execution balanced against restrained parallel processing capability. The server achieved 1,826.99 in single-core stress-ng tests and 1,391.0 in Geekbench single-core evaluations, placing within the median 50% band of general cloud hardware. In contrast, multi-threaded results were restricted by the two-core physical topology, scoring 3,848.4 in multi-core stress-ng and 2,970.0 in Geekbench multi-core, which sit in the lower 25% bracket. Memory throughput registered 30.16 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 25.23 GB/sec for uncached write operations. Application-level metrics reflect these hardware boundaries, producing 3.89 million Redis SET operations per second, 4.8 GB/sec in static web serving, and 98.81 tokens per second during lightweight 135M-parameter language model text generation.

The resource ratio and execution profile position ecs.u1-c1m2.xlarge as a cost-efficient platform for light to moderate compute tasks that do not require extensive memory capacity or local I/O speed. The 1:2 memory proportion makes it suitable for low-overhead application layers, background automation, software compilation workers, API gateways, and non-production staging environments. Workloads requiring memory-intensive in-memory data grids, large database transaction processing, or heavy parallel computing may face memory pressure and parallelization bottlenecks, making higher-tier general-purpose or memory-optimized configurations more appropriate.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m2.xlarge is an x86_64 virtual machine built on KVM virtualization within the provider's general-purpose utility tier. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.5 GHz with hyper-threading enabled, accompanied by 8.0 GB of system memory at a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The processor includes standard extensions such as AVX, AVX-512, and AES, supported by 33 MB of Level 3 cache. The instance features a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operates without integrated local storage, and includes no GPUs. Benchmark metrics reveal moderate single-threaded capability, achieving average scores in Geekbench and stress-ng single-core tests, whereas multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth place in the lower quartile. Consequently, ecs.u1-c1m2.xlarge delivers cost-efficient resource allocation for moderate, non-bursting compute tasks, including microservices, CI/CD runners, internal proxy servers, lightweight caching nodes, and continuous development staging workloads.
